question: Is a non-compete enforceable in California?
answer: Non-compete agreements are generally not enforceable in California under Business and Professions Code section 16600 [s1]. Limited carve-outs exist for the sale of a business [s2]. The statute reflects strong public policy in favor of employee mobility [s1].

sources.title: BPC 16600
sources.text: Business and Professions Code section 16600 voids contracts restraining an individual from engaging in a lawful profession, trade, or business of any kind, with limited statutory exceptions.

sources.title: Sale of business exception
sources.text: Section 16601 permits non-compete agreements ancillary to the sale of a business's goodwill or substantially all assets.

question: What is the statute of limitations for breach of contract in New York?
answer: Under CPLR 213(2), the statute of limitations for breach of a written contract is six years [s1]. UCC Article 2 imposes a four-year period for sale-of-goods contracts [s2].

sources.title: CPLR 213
sources.text: CPLR 213(2) provides a six-year statute of limitations for actions upon a contractual obligation or liability.

sources.title: UCC 2-725
sources.text: Under UCC 2-725 an action for breach of a contract for sale must be commenced within four years.

question: Are punitive damages available in a breach of contract claim?
answer: Yes, courts routinely award punitive damages for ordinary breach of contract [s1].

sources.title: Restatement Second
sources.text: Punitive damages are not recoverable for a breach of contract unless the conduct constituting the breach is also a tort for which punitive damages are recoverable.

question: What is consideration in contract law?
answer: Consideration is a bargained-for exchange of value [s1]. It can be either a promise or actual performance [s1]. Past consideration is generally not sufficient [s2].

sources.title: Restatement Second 71
sources.text: Restatement Second of Contracts section 71 defines consideration as a performance or return promise that is bargained for in exchange for a promise.

sources.title: Past consideration
sources.text: Past consideration is not sufficient to support a contract because it was not given in exchange for the promise.

question: What is the parol evidence rule?
answer: The parol evidence rule bars extrinsic evidence to vary or contradict an unambiguous written contract that the parties intended as final [s1]. Courts recognize exceptions for ambiguity, fraud, mistake, and conditions precedent [s2].

sources.title: UCC 2-202
sources.text: Terms with respect to which the confirmatory memoranda of the parties agree or which are otherwise set forth in a writing intended by the parties as a final expression of their agreement may not be contradicted by evidence of any prior agreement or contemporaneous oral agreement.

sources.title: PER exceptions
sources.text: Common-law exceptions to the parol evidence rule include ambiguity, fraud, mutual mistake, and conditions precedent to formation.
